newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria shares end easier, U.S. data dominates.
newsitem.headline: Austria shares end easier, U.S. data dominates.

text.p: Austrian shares closed marginally lower on Friday just ahead of eagerly awaited U.S. employment data.
The blue-chip ATX index ended 1.09 points, or 0.09 percent, down at 1,167.80 after trading in a narrow 1,163.11 to 1,170.67 points range in moderate turnover.
Dealers said ATX support at 1,160 points looked secure.

"The Vienna market has until Monday to decide how it will react to the U.S. figures," a trader said, noting that other European stock markets had spiked higher on a slightly lower-than-expected 175,000 rise in March non-farm payrolls.
Unemployment of 5.2 percent was in line with expectations.
Six ATX shares finished lower, 12 higher and three unchanged.
Steelmaker VA Stahl, which on Thursday reported a 45 percent drop in 1996 net profit and said it expected a similar 1997 result, was the leading decliner and by far the most actively traded stock.
Its shares ended 3.07 percent down at 450 schillings on 158,724 contracts.
"VA Stahl broke through some strong support lines. Now the share has room all the way down to 430 or 420 schillings," a trader said.
Market participants said most of the sell-orders could be traced to large institutional investors.
Fibre-maker Lenzing was the top gainer, up 3.0 percent to 618 schillings.
In continuous trade but outside the ATX, water treatment company continued its bull run, chalking up a new year high for the third straight day.
BWT, which unveiled new sales-enhancing technology last month, finished 43 schillings up at 1,750.
April ATX futures stood 4.5 points up at 1,167.5 on turnover of 508 contracts. The broad-based Vienna bourse index slipped 0.04 points to 444.26.
